findings.expected: Top-10 voter/validator share and HHI (or delegated share) measured from a dated snapshot; top-4 validators/delegates hold under 1/3 of voting power
findings.observed: Top-4 bonded validators hold 37.98% of bonded stake — over the 1/3 Tendermint liveness threshold. Top-1 18.79% (Coinbase01), top-10 56.49%, HHI 0.0578, from the 2026-11-10 bonded-validators snapshot (180 validators).

findings.expected: Delay >= 1 day, stated in docs
findings.observed: No timelock: a passed proposal executes through the chain (upgrade at a scheduled height, or the message executes on passage). There is no mandatory execution delay after the vote closes.

findings.control: No observed treasury transfer outside DAO recall
findings.expected: No executed proposal moved funds to an address the DAO cannot recall
findings.observed: Proposal 1058 passed and moved 1,227,121 ATOM recovered after the Neutron exploit to the Neutron recovery multisig — funds the DAO cannot recall at its own discretion. Proposal 1060 similarly routes community-pool USDC through a community multisig.

findings.expected: Explicit max actions per proposal (e.g. 10)
findings.observed: No maximum number of messages per proposal is stated in the live gov params or the Cosmos SDK gov spec; proposals in the window carry one message type each, but multi-message proposals are not bounded by a documented cap.

findings.expected: Delay >= 1 day, stated in docs
findings.observed: No voting delay: once a proposal reaches the 500 ATOM minimum deposit it enters the voting period immediately. The deposit period (up to 14 days) is the only review window, and it can be as short as the time to fund the deposit.

findings.expected: Winning option must exceed the runner-up by a stated margin
findings.observed: No vote-differential rule: a proposal passes on >50% yes (excluding abstain) plus 40% quorum. The 33.4% veto threshold is a rejection rule, not a winning-margin rule.

findings.expected: Expiry window stated in docs
findings.observed: No grace period: Cosmos Hub governance has no expiry window for passed proposals; the concept does not exist in the gov module.

findings.expected: Documented limits: cannot seize funds, cannot unpause, cannot upgrade
findings.observed: Limits on emergency/cancel powers were not verified from a primary source; the cancel parameter exists but its bounds are undocumented in the fetched sources.

findings.control: Proposer must maintain delegated power through voting
findings.expected: Contract cancels the proposal if the proposer falls below threshold
findings.observed: No proposer-maintenance rule in the OpenZeppelin Governor used by ENS: nothing cancels a proposal if the proposer falls below 100,000 ENS delegated during voting (EP 5.15 discusses only the voting delay, not proposer maintenance).

findings.expected: Delay >= 1 day, stated in docs
findings.observed: Voting delay is 1 block (EP 5.15: 'the voting delay period which is currently set to only one block'). EP 5.15 proposes a 24-hour delay; not yet in force at snapshot date.

findings.expected: Winning option must exceed the runner-up by a stated margin
findings.observed: No vote-differential rule: executable proposals pass on a simple majority plus the 1% quorum. The two-thirds rule for constitutional amendments is an approval threshold, not a differential.

findings.expected: Top-10 voter/validator share and HHI (or delegated share) measured from a dated snapshot; top-4 validators/delegates hold under 1/3 of voting power
findings.observed: Delegated share measured: 3,980,000 ENS of 100,000,000 (3.98%) delegated (Tally, 2026-11-10). Per-delegate / top-holder concentration (HHI) not measured: Tally delegate voting powers were not captured in the snapshot — disclosed as a limitation.

findings.control: Upgrade authority path documented and controlled
findings.expected: Who can upgrade the governance contracts / chain (and at what height or delay) is stated in a primary source and the path requires a passed governance proposal
findings.observed: Upgrade path is via passed executable proposals through the governor/timelock (docs: executable proposals can upgrade an ENS core contract), but the controlling authority for the ENS root and the pending Governor Nexus changes were not verified as a single documented path.

findings.control: Treasury moves only via timelocked governance
findings.expected: Treasury controlled only through the timelock
findings.observed: Treasury moves mostly via timelocked governance, but the Treasury Flow Automation proposal grants Karpatkey a scoped permission to send ETH/USDC to wallet.ensdao.eth without a proposal; the timelock keeps a 6-month USDC runway (~$8M).

findings.control: All lifecycle parameters published in official docs
findings.expected: Every parameter (threshold, quorum, delay, period, timelock, grace) stated
findings.observed: Voting delay (1 block) is stated only in EP 5.15, not in the main governance-process doc; the timelock grace period is not stated anywhere in ENS docs.

findings.control: No unresolved parameter discrepancy across primary sources
findings.expected: All primary sources agree on all parameters
findings.observed: Direct discrepancy: docs.ens.domains/dao/security-council states a 4-of-8 council, while EP 6.50 (July 2026) seated a 5-of-8 council for a term to 2028-07-16.

findings.control: Standing bounds / whitelists on treasury operations
findings.expected: Explicit per-operation bounds or whitelists
findings.observed: Each treasury/community-pool transfer needs its own vote; no standing per-operation bounds or whitelists were found in the live params or the sampled proposals.

findings.control: Emergency pause / cancel power exists and is documented
findings.expected: Pause and/or cancel power documented
findings.observed: Only the proposal_cancel_ratio parameter (0.5) hints at a cancel path; its semantics were not verified from a primary source. No documented emergency pause power for governance exists.

findings.expected: Any address can lock a small amount to create an autonomous proposal, or equivalent
findings.observed: No live autonomous/bond proposal path. EP 5.15 (social, passed) approves a 1,000 ENS ProposalBond design in principle; it is not implemented, so the 100,000 ENS threshold remains the only gate.

findings.expected: Explicit max actions per proposal (e.g. 10)
findings.observed: No explicit max actions per proposal stated in ENS docs. Payloads are bounded in practice only by block gas limits; no stated max verified.

findings.expected: Expiry window stated in docs
findings.observed: No grace period stated in ENS docs for the OpenZeppelin TimelockController; whether queued operations expire was not verified from a primary source at audit time.

findings.control: Standing bounds / whitelists on treasury operations
findings.expected: Explicit per-operation bounds or whitelists
findings.observed: Standing bound exists in part: the Treasury Flow Automation policy keeps a 6-month runway (~$8M USDC) in the timelock. No per-operation whitelist or cap schedule was verified.

findings.expected: Multisig threshold and signers published
findings.observed: New council members are named individuals (EP 6.50) and the 5-of-8 threshold is published, but the official docs page still describes the expired 4-of-8 council, so the published composition is inconsistent across primary sources.

findings.control: Veto / cancel authority is time-bounded with a renewal path
findings.expected: Cancel/veto authority carries an expiry and a documented renewal path (re-vote / re-election)
findings.observed: New council term runs to 2028-07-16 with an expiry mechanism carried from the 2024 design, but the docs page still describes the old council whose authority expired 2026-07-24; the renewal path was demonstrated (EP 6.45 defeated, EP 6.50 re-founded) rather than documented as a rule.
